text:
maria: Observed a new perf regression on staging: a lot of decode batches are being torn down while tool/function calls are in-flight, which is triggering expensive kernel swaps and KV eviction. Impacting p50 by ~12ms and p99 by ~70ms.
cheng: Can you paste the profiler dump? suspect kernel selection thrash when pause > 30ms.
maria: Dump attached below (summarized). note: these are continuous-batching workers on a8x pools.
```
[profiling] decode_batcher: batch_size=8 -> form_time=6ms -> wait_for_tool_pause=42ms -> kernel_swap=true
[kernel] prev=amp_float16_opt next=quant8_fast => swap_cost=35ms
[kv] evicted_prefixes=12 kv_gc_ms=14
```

maria: TL;DR: tool pause durations exceed our token-budget window, batcher abandons batch, runtime swaps kernels to a quantized exec path (incompatible with current kv layout) and we pay the swap + KV rehydrate.
nate: Oof. That matches a repro I ran. Structured output + stop-token scanning increases pause variance. If pause_prob > 0.03 we start seeing >30ms tail.
kevin: Two levers: 1) bias kernel selection to prefer non-swap compat modes for short-lived batches 2) change queue policy to allow short hold-window when toolcall detected so prefix KV stays hot.
sara: SLA question: how will changing hold-window affect latency SLOs vs throughput? we need a small experiment plan.
cheng: Proposal: adaptive hold-window that observes toolcall hint metadata and extends hold_window by min( max_pause_est, 50ms ). Also lower token-budget-trigger from 16 tokens to 8 for toolcall-tagged requests so we don't prematurely form tiny batches that force swaps.
maria: Quick config prototype I tested locally:
```
# runtime config snippet
batching:
  default_hold_ms: 6
  toolcall_hint:
    extra_hold_ms: 50
    token_budget_trigger: 8
kernel:
  prefer_stable_for_toolcall: true
```

maria: Results from local A/B (100k requests): p50 improved 8ms, p99 improved 28ms, throughput -1.7% (expected due to hold window). KV eviction drops 3x.
nate: Nice. Two follow-ups: add a safety cap so if hold_window causes queue growth > 250ms we revert on that worker; and record a telemetry metric for "kernel_swap_reason" to validate the hypothesis in prod.
kevin: I'll take the safe-circuit patch. adding a worker-side circuit-breaker + metric. also want a small e2e that injects long stop-token scans to verify.
cheng: For rollout: start on 10% dedicated capacity GPUs (non-critical), monitor p99 and queue depth. If queue depth > 200ms for >5m, auto-roll back.
sara: Sounds acceptable. please add runbook notes re: how to rollback and how to interpret kernel_swap_reason metric.
maria: I'll open a PR with config + runbook + perf dashboard. tagging @cheng @kevin for review. :thumbsup:
